title: OSHA Confined Space Checklist (29 CFR 1910.146)
subtitle: Use at each permit-required confined space before authorizing entry and during the work.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Record each Defect, tell the entry supervisor, and correct it before entry begins or continues.
Your permit space program, equipment manufacturers' instructions and site rules may add checks.

sections.title: Space identification and program
items: This space has been evaluated and classified as permit-required or non-permit.
A danger sign or equally effective means at the space tells employees it is a permit space and what the danger is.
The program's measures to prevent unauthorized entry are in place at this space.
The written permit space program is available for employees and their representatives to inspect.
The hazards of this space were identified and evaluated before anyone entered.
Any change in use or configuration that might increase hazards has led to a reevaluation of the space.
Any contractor entering has been told the site has permit spaces and entry requires a compliant program.

sections.title: Permit and roles
items: A permit for this entry was prepared and issued under the site's written permit system.
The acceptable entry conditions for this space are specified.
At least one attendant is outside the space for the whole entry.
If the attendant covers more than one space, the program sets out how they respond to an emergency in any of them.
Entrants, attendant, entry supervisor and testers on this entry are designated, know their duties and have had the required training.
Communications equipment is provided and working for contact between entrants and the attendant.
Where entrants from more than one employer work at once, coordination procedures are in use.

sections.title: Atmosphere, isolation and equipment
items: Conditions were tested and found acceptable before entry was authorized.
Oxygen was tested first, then combustible gases and vapors, then toxic gases and vapors.
The space is tested or monitored as needed to show acceptable conditions are maintained.
Entrants or their representatives were offered the chance to watch the testing.
Test results were given to entrants or their representatives as soon as they were available.
The space is isolated, for example by blanking, double block and bleed or lockout, as the program requires.
Purging, inerting, flushing or ventilating is done as necessary to eliminate or control atmospheric hazards.
Pedestrian, vehicle or other barriers protect entrants from outside hazards where needed.
Lighting lets entrants see well enough to work safely and exit quickly in an emergency.
Ladders or other equipment for safe entry and exit are in place.

sections.title: Rescue and close-out
items: A procedure for calling rescue and emergency services is in place and known to the entry team.
A procedure for getting entrants out of this space is in place.
Procedures stop unauthorized personnel from attempting a rescue.
The employer has provided the rescue and emergency equipment the rescue procedures need, except to the extent the rescue service provides it.
Conditions are checked and stay acceptable for the full duration of the entry.
After the work, the space is closed off and the permit canceled under the concluding procedure.
Any unauthorized entry, uncovered hazard, prohibited condition, injury or near-miss led to a program review before the next entry.

references: 29 CFR 1910.146: Permit-required confined spaces (OSHA general industry)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, Part 1910, Subpart J
